//: EASY CONFIG (Spanish, Spain). Travel-first order: survival -> numbers -> food -> getting around -> money/shopping -> hotel -> extra words -> conversation. Word lessons sit directly before the phrase lessons that use them. Entries marked (staff) / (you'll hear) are for recognition. Requests to strangers use usted; in Spain tu is also common with younger staff.
name: Spanish

lessons.title: How Spanish Sounds
lessons.//: Spanish is written as it sounds. These few rules let you read every entry.

entries.note: h is always silent.
In Spain, c before e/i sounds like English 'th'.
z and c (before e/i) both sound like 'th' in Spain.
j is a throaty h, like 'ch' in Scottish 'loch'.
g before e/i sounds like j.
ll sounds like English 'y'.
ñ sounds like 'ny' in 'canyon'.
rr is rolled; single r is a quick tap. It changes the meaning.
b and v sound the same.
qu = k. The u is silent.
An accent mark shows the stressed syllable. Questions start with ¿, exclamations with ¡.
